designAuthority.source: Accepted MFR-002 U07 contract plus read-only live Figma Design and Figma Make context for the authenticated Lending and Release workspaces

change.lending: The authenticated Internal Lending Hub now presents loaded lifecycle navigation for review, claim, loan, overdue, and terminal records while retaining server paging and protected borrower scope.
change.lendingConsequences: Review, issue/handoff, and return dialogs show the exact record, person, item, quantity, protected identity or evidence basis, and custody consequence before the governed action. Invalid quantities, assignments, and return reconciliation state that no custody update occurs.
change.release: The Release Desk is a focused ready-record station: select one authoritative line, identify the recipient, choose a whole-number quantity, select governed evidence, review the exact consequence, acknowledge it, and trigger a fresh authorized recheck before any evidence upload or release command.
change.truthBoundary: The client stops when the ready line, request/item identity, unit, revision, requested/released/remaining quantity, status, or requested release quantity changes. It neither invents stock, reservation, custody, ledger, audit, or receipt success nor assumes a release after a failed command.
change.partialAndCumulative: Partial and full remaining release consequences are explicit; history does not sum quantities across mixed units; existing server-owned cumulative release and return behavior remains authoritative.
change.idempotencyAndEvidence: Release command identity is tied to the exact rechecked line state and user-entered custody facts. Governed evidence retry identity includes the request, line, file metadata, MIME type, and SHA-256 file-content digest so distinct files with matching metadata are not conflated.
change.architecture: Release derivation, recheck/consequence rules, history presentation, and shared operational utilities were separated from the route container. The authenticated route chunk grew 3,683 gzip bytes; an additional lazy boundary was rejected because that small authenticated-only cost did not earn more loading and failure states.

performance.measurementProfile: U06 and U07 canonical Vite application artifacts built from the same dependency graph; direct transfer uses entry HTML plus only its referenced CSS and JavaScript, compressed with Node zlib level 9.

accessibility.lendingInspector: At 320, 390, and 768 CSS pixels, selection is a modal dialog with initial focus, Tab containment, Escape, inert background, body scroll restoration, and opener focus restoration. At 1024 and 1440 CSS pixels it is a persistent nonmodal complementary inspector.
accessibility.consequentialDialogs: Lending review, handoff/issue, return, and Release confirmation are labelled modal dialogs with contained focus, inert shell regions, Escape or explicit close behavior, and consequences before the submit action.
accessibility.releaseConfirmation: The acknowledgement checkbox receives initial focus; the final action stays disabled until acknowledgement; Escape restores the Review release consequence opener; shell navigation and route content are inert while the modal is open.
accessibility.lifecycleAndStatus: Lifecycle controls expose pressed state and exact loaded counts; status meaning is text-backed and uses semantic theme tokens rather than color alone.
accessibility.themeAndMotion: Semantic status, notice, surface, and consequence tokens preserve the six theme families and twelve Light/Dark appearances; existing reduced-motion and forced-colors behavior remains supported.

renderedBrowser.attempt: The frontend-390 U07 Release journey was launched and stopped before rendering because the project-pinned Chromium executable is absent.
renderedBrowser.notClaimed: No fresh rendered five-width, keyboard, 200 percent reflow, focus-obscuration, visual-regression, Web Vitals, INP, route-ready, or live API latency PASS is claimed for U07.
fallbackEvidence: The Lending and Release matrix enumerates 45 cases across 320, 390, 768, 1024, and 1440 CSS-pixel projects; the complete frontend configuration enumerates 485 tests.

Focused unit contracts cover lifecycle grouping, partial/full/invalid release consequences, cumulative candidates, missing/changed authoritative state, history mapping, and cryptographic evidence content identity.

Source-level Playwright contracts assert exact five-fact consequences, mobile dialog versus desktop complementary semantics, inert background, focus restoration, authoritative recheck before evidence upload, stale-state stop behavior, receipt/history reload, and no generic collection clutter.
Canonical and staging React artifacts compile through Vite and pass fixture-boundary, design, contrast, normal-asset, deploy-marker, and byte-identical hero gates.

rollback: Revert the isolated U07 commit. No migration, index, backend, provider, deployment, or data rollback is required.
